name: Aksumite state paganism (Mahrem/Astar/Beher-Meder)

dating.dating_summary: Attested almost entirely from epigraphy and coinage at the very end of the tradition's history (Ezana's own pre-conversion inscriptions, likely 330s CE, and the Monumentum Adulitanum, original date uncertain 2nd-3rd c. CE, surviving only via a 6th-century copy) — no scriptural corpus, no earlier evidence of comparable specificity survives.

earliest_archaeological_evidence.note: Aksumite coinage bearing disc-and-crescent symbolism from King Endubis, c. 270-300 CE, is the primary chronological anchor for early Aksumite religious material culture.

earliest_written_attestation.note: Ezana's own pre-Christian Ge'ez inscriptions (catalogued RIÉ 185 I/II = DAE 6-7), likely 330s CE, name the triad Mahrem/Astar/Beher(or Meder) directly.

surviving_manuscript_date.note: The Monumentum Adulitanum (equating Mahrem/Beher/Meder with Ares/Poseidon/Zeus) survives only via a copy made by the monk Cosmas Indicopleustes at Adulis c. 518-525 CE, published in his Christian Topography (c. 547-549 CE); the original stone is lost and its own composition date is only estimated (2nd-3rd century CE, attributed to an unnamed pre-Ezana king).

tradition_internal_claim.note: N/A — no continuous adherent community survives to assert an origin claim.

estimated_oral_origin.method: Comparative Semitic-religion scholarship situates the astral/war-god cult type within a South Arabian religious koine attested in Saba' from the early-to-mid 1st millennium BCE; the earlier, distinct Kingdom of D'mt (~8th-5th c. BCE, same region) shows related Almaqah worship, but bridging D'mt to Aksum religiously is inference, not documented continuity.

notes: Mahrem (war god; Aksumite kings styled themselves "son of the invincible Mahrem"); Astar (astral character disputed — Venus-analog vs. sun/moon deity, sources disagree); Beher/Meder (sea/sky, earth). Comparison of Mahrem to South Arabian Almaqah is repeatedly made in secondary literature but the degree of identity is explicitly uncertain — do not assert equivalence.
